concepts.name: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation
concepts.summary: The fine-tuning update is approximated as a low-rank product: DELTA-W ~= B . A, with A of shape r x d and B of shape d x r and inner rank r << d. The base weight W is frozen and only A, B are trained; at use the correction slots straight in, W_new = W + B . A. For d=1000, r=8 this is 16,000 trained numbers against 1,000,000 for a full DELTA-W (62x fewer).

concepts.name: The Low-Rank Update
concepts.summary: LoRA's wager: the meaningful change during fine-tuning lives in a small subspace, so DELTA-W has low effective rank and can be written as B . A with a small inner rank r. It is a bet, confirmed by training, not a proof; too small an r cannot fit the task.

concepts.name: Frozen Base Weights
concepts.summary: The pretrained weight W is frozen: no gradient flows into it, it is trained once and shared unchanged across every adaptation. Only the tiny A, B pair is trained and stored, so each adapted model is a few-megabyte adapter resting on one shared base, not a full copy.
